title: CI/CD token theft
overview: Review a workflow token-use audit projection when privileged actions come from an unapproved runner pool.
prerequisites: Know the basics of CI/CD auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Application Access Token
attack.rationale: T1550.001 applies to use of an application access token. The sample does not show theft itself.

hypothesis: Repository-write token use on an unapproved runner should be correlated to workflow identity and job context.
evidence: Review runner pool, scope, workflow and actor. Match to an expected job and inspect resulting repository actions.
false_positive: A scheduled migration to a new runner pool can look anomalous before inventory catches up.
tuning: Join runner identity and policy history. Review write permissions separately from read-only builds.
response: Stop the affected workflow through approved controls, revoke the credential or session and review resulting changes.
prevention: Prefer short-lived workload identity and narrowly scoped job tokens. Require approved runner images and pools.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The event contains no authentication material. It models suspicious use, not token acquisition.

questions.explanation: Write privileges can modify content or production configuration.

options: Runner, workflow, job and repository actions
questions.explanation: A known job should explain the privilege and observed operation.
